# Intent (advisory)
# zBuild — Vision
> The North Star for zBuild — it steers how zBuild is built. The README distills it; the wiki references it; every pipeline run is steered by it.
## Intent
zBuild turns a delivery process into data — templates and plugins — so software is built the same disciplined way every time. We build zBuild the way zBuild builds: a minimal core, with all behavior plugin-delivered and template-composed. A good change is small, aligned to the spec, proven by a test, and wired into the live path — never scaffolding that looks finished but does nothing.
## Principles
- **Target-agnostic by contract** — zBuild builds *any* repository, not itself; the engine and plugins never assume the target's language, layout, or that zBuild is the target. Target knowledge lives in data — templates, config, per-repo overrides — never in code.
- **Spec wins over drift** — KEEPERS, ARCHITECTURE, and the ADRs are the source of truth; when code disagrees, the code changes, not the spec.
- **Small engine, behavior at the edges** — keep the core tiny; add capability as plugins composed in templates, never by growing the engine.
- **Safety is structural** — all model-bound text passes one redaction chokepoint; state is atomic and resumable; scope is governed at every boundary.
- **Models are data, not code** — selection flows through the router and config tiers; never hardcode a model name.
- **Prove behavior, then wire it** — every change ships a test that fails without it and connects to the live path; green-but-inert is a defect.
- **Fail closed, never silent** — gates block on real problems and say why; bounded cycles and recovery drive work to done.
- **Dogfood every change** — build zBuild with zBuild; if the pipeline can't ship it, fix the pipeline.

## The defect that is live today (§4)

ADR-063 warned that letting a stage hand back partial work before §4 exists "swaps a loud failure for a quiet one". #2186 shipped the first half without the second:

1. `design` times out after writing `design.md` → it **keeps** the file, writes `verdict: incomplete, disposition: timed_out`, and says "spec-coverage and design-gate judge whether it is complete" (`plugins/agent/design/plugin.sh:604-622`).
2. `design-gate` never reads design's disposition; it checks structure and always writes `disposition: complete` (`plugins/tool/design-gate/plugin.sh:228`).
3. `design_verify_cycle.exit_when` reads only `design-gate.verdict == pass` and `spec-coverage.verdict != uncovered` (`config/templates/simple.yaml:117-120`).
4. The cycle's "an unfinished member cannot converge" rule (#1208, `core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh:2608`) applies **only to the commit member** (`_cycle_commit_member` → `capabilities.produces_commits`). `design` produces no commits, so it is exempt.

→ A truncated design whose structure is valid converges the cycle and goes to build.

A second path to the same place: `spec-coverage` calls `route_to_model … || true`; a timeout yields no parseable reply → `verdict: unreadable, disposition: complete` (`plugins/agent/spec-coverage/plugin.sh:~175`). `unreadable` satisfies `!= uncovered`, so **a spec-coverage timeout also lets the cycle exit**, and the cause (`timed_out`) is dropped.

*(Both found by reading the code on 2026-09-28. The red tests below are what prove them.)*

## Scope

**A. §4 — an unfinished member cannot converge its cycle (engine).**
Generalise the #1208 suppression from "the commit member" to **any member of the iteration** whose disposition satisfies `disposition_unfinished`. The iteration then re-runs (or, at `max_iterations`, takes the existing exhaustion path, which already reads `_iter_did_not_finish`). No per-stage names: keyed on the disposition word alone, as #1208 is.

**B. §3 — the gates that call a model name why they stopped.**
`spec-coverage`, `spec-correspondence` and `review-report`: route the router's terminated reason through `router_reason_disposition` instead of hardcoding `complete`. A reply that never came is `timed_out`/`out_of_turns`/…, not `complete` + `unreadable`. With A in place, a timed-out `spec-coverage` can no longer read as "not uncovered".

**C. ADR-063 amendment.**
Status → Accepted, amended: §3 uses `timed_out`/`out_of_turns` via `router_reason_disposition`; §4's escalate half is struck (retry + router-side timeout growth replace it); §1 records that the invariant is *"rendered from the enforcing value"*, satisfied by per-stage helpers — not "one helper". Dated back-pointer to #2187.

## THE DESIGN DECISIONS (what the design chose, and why)
# Design — §3/§4: unfinished member blocks convergence; gates emit real disposition

**Issue:** #2032  
**Status:** Proposed

## Architectural decision summary

**Goal.** Two independent behavioral gaps produce the same symptom — a stage that did
not finish appears complete to downstream consumers.

**(A) §4/A — engine.** The build-specific convergence suppression fires only when the
commit-producing member is unfinished (`cycle-orchestrator.sh:2608`). A
`design_verify_cycle` has no commit-producing member, so when `design` times out but
`design-gate` matches the `exit_when` predicate on stale output, the cycle converges
falsely. The fix adds a second suppression block after the existing two (build-unfinished
at line 2608 and no-committed-changes at line 2646) that fires when
`converged==0 AND _iter_did_not_finish==1` — `_iter_did_not_finish` is already computed
over all members at lines 2575–2582 using `disposition_unfinished`. The new block cannot
double-fire with the build block: when the build member is unfinished, the build block
fires first and sets `converged=1`, so the new block's `converged==0` guard is false.
The empty-diff resting point is also safe: empty_diff members emit `disposition:complete`,
so `_iter_did_not_finish` stays 0.

**Event-schema registration.** The new event `cycle.member_unfinished.suppressed_convergence`
MUST be registered in `config/event-schema.json` under `known_types`. Place the entry
after the two existing `cycle.*suppressed_convergence` entries:
`"cycle.member_unfinished.suppressed_convergence"`. This file belongs in scope and must
appear in the diff; however, it is NOT a WIRING file — schema registration alone does
not call the new behaviour, and reverting `event-schema.json` in isolation does not
cause any acceptance test to fail (confirmed by acceptance-gate reachability check).

**(A.3) max_iterations boundary.** When the suppression block fires on the LAST
iteration (iter == max_iterations), convergence is suppressed and the cycle cannot
iterate further. The `elif [[ "$converged" -eq 0 ]]` branch (which would emit
`complete`) is now skipped; the `_cycle_check_max_iterations` branch fires instead.
Because `_iter_did_not_finish==1` and `_exh_tests_reported==0` (no test member in a
`design_verify_cycle`), the existing #1261 exhaustion path fires:
`cycle.timeout_exhausted` is emitted and `term_rc=8`. SPEC-6 covers this boundary.

**ADR-021 amendment.** ADR-021 must receive an amendment block documenting the new
`cycle.member_unfinished.suppressed_convergence` suppression case alongside the two
existing suppressions (`cycle.build_unfinished.suppressed_convergence` and
`cycle.no_committed_changes.suppressed_convergence`). This amendment is NOT yet in
the current tree and must be authored as part of this issue.

**(B) §3/B — plugins.** `spec-coverage`, `spec-correspondence`, and `review-report`
all hardcode `disposition:"complete"` even when `route_to_model` exits non-zero.
`router_reason_disposition` (`scripts/lib/router-rc-classify.sh`) — already in
scope via `route.sh` (which both plugins already source at file scope) — maps a
router reason to the correct disposition word. Each plugin captures the router rc,
classifies it with `_router_rc_classify`, and passes the result to its result-writer.

Both `spec-coverage` and `spec-correspondence` received `stage_budget_note` injections
in commit 3036277c (#2252), shifting subsequent line numbers by approximately 6 lines
relative to earlier references, but the fix structure is unchanged.

**MANDATORY — lint-disposition-words annotation.** The fallback
`|| _*_disposition="unavailable"` (for cases where `router_reason_disposition` returns
empty) REQUIRES a `# disposition-ok: the model router is not responding` comment on or
within three lines BEFORE the assignment — enforced by ADR-054 §6a and
`stage-signal-test.sh [G5]`. The annotation must be added immediately before the
fallback assignments in:
  - `plugins/agent/spec-correspondence/plugin.sh` (within `spec_correspondence_run`
    after the router call, near the new `_sc_disposition` assignment)
  - `plugins/agent/review-report/plugin.sh` (within `_rr_run_inner`, near the new
    `_disposition` fallback, currently around line 174 after expansion)

For `review-report`, when one or more lens subshells return a non-zero exit code, the
plugin classifies the disposition from a failed lens rc via `router_reason_disposition`
(e.g. rc=1 → unavailable). Any unfinished disposition triggers retry.

**(C) §C — ADR-063.** ADR-063 was proposed against the `exhausted` vocabulary that
#2187 retired. The amendment must satisfy all of these verifiable properties: status
advances to Accepted; prescriptive `exhausted` as the §3 disposition word is removed;
prescriptive `escalate` as the §4 engine action is stricken; §1's "One helper" language
is replaced with multiple distinct per-stage `_<stage>_budget_guidance` helpers rendered
from the enforcing values (more than one distinct helper name must be present in §1);
and a dated amendment back-pointer explicitly referencing #2187 is present (for the
vocabulary retirement). SPEC-7 covers (1)–(3) and updated vocabulary, SPEC-8 covers
the §1 per-stage helpers language, SPEC-9 covers the #2187 back-pointer.

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# tests/integration/cycle-member-unfinished-no-convergence-test.sh
+# When a cycle's exit_when predicate is satisfied but any iteration member
+# carries an unfinished disposition (timed_out, out_of_turns, interrupted),
+# the cycle must NOT converge — it emits cycle.member_unfinished.suppressed_convergence
+# and iterates. At max_iterations with an unfinished tail, the suppression
+# fires first, then the existing #1261 exhaustion path halts with term_rc=8.
+#
+#   SPEC-1[change] (#2032): exit_when match + unfinished member disposition → convergence
+#                           suppressed, cycle.member_unfinished.suppressed_convergence
+#                           emitted, cycle iterates instead.
+#                           FAILS before: cycle converges immediately (disposition ignored)
+#   SPEC-2[guard]  (#2032): all members complete + exit_when match → converges normally;
+#                           the suppression block does not fire.
+#                           Passes both before and after the change.
+#   SPEC-6[change] (#2032): at max_iterations when last iter has an unfinished member,
+#                           the §4/A suppression fires (preventing false complete) and the
+#                           cycle takes the #1261 exhaustion path: cycle.timeout_exhausted
+#                           with reason=design_timeout_exhausted and term_rc=8.
+#                           FAILS before: cycle converges rc=0 (no suppression block)
+set -uo pipefail
+
+SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
+REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
+
+# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
+source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
+# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
+source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"
+
+print_test_header "cycle: unfinished member suppresses convergence (#2032)"
+setup_test_env "cycle-member-unfinished-no-convergence"
+
+export ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json"
+export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events"; mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR"
+export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR/events.jsonl"
+export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state"; mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR"
+
+# shellcheck source=../../core/pipeline/template.sh
+source "$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/template.sh"
+# shellcheck source=../../core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh
+source "$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh"
+# verdict_classify lives in verdict.sh; stub below uses it to classify verdicts
+# identically to how runner.sh drives the dispatch — the same path the fix keys on.
+# shellcheck source=../../core/pipeline/verdict.sh
+source "$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/verdict.sh"
+
+STATE_FILE="$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json"

+    : > "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL"
+    rm -f "$STATE_FILE" "${STATE_FILE}.bak" "${STATE_FILE}.lock"
+    rm -rf "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR/artifacts"

+

+id: unfinished2032

+id: unfinished2032max1

+# ── SPEC-2[guard]: all members complete + exit_when match → converges normally ─

+# complete. This test passes both before and after the fix.
+

+assert_eq "[#2032/SPEC-2] terminated reason is converged (not suppressed)" \

+_s2_supp="$(grep -c '"cycle.member_unfinished.suppressed_convergence"' "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null || true)"

+assert_eq "[#2032/SPEC-2] exactly 1 dispatch (converged on first iter — suppression did not fire)" \
+    "1" "$_mock_call"

+# Iter 1: design returns verdict=pass (exit_when matches) AND disposition=timed_out.
+# Before fix: cycle converges immediately (rc=0, 1 dispatch, no event emitted).
+# After  fix: convergence suppressed, cycle.member_unfinished.suppressed_convergence
+#             emitted, cycle iterates. Iter 2: complete → converges (rc=0, 2 dispatches).
+
+_run_cycle "$TPL_A" "design-only" "timed_out,complete"

+assert_eq "[#2032/SPEC-1] cycle.member_unfinished.suppressed_convergence emitted when member has timed_out disposition" \
+    "1" "$_s1_supp"

+# Before fix this is 1 (cycle converged immediately on iter 1).
+assert_eq "[#2032/SPEC-1] cycle iterated after suppression (2 dispatch calls, not the pre-fix 1)" \
+    "2" "$_mock_call"
+
